title: The Withheld Payout
logline: An insurance company buys the telemetry drive of a wrecked ship to hide their liability, leaving the deceased pilot's child to fight for the truth.

roles.description: Grieving, broke, but stubbornly refusing to let their parent be blamed for a mechanical failure.
Pragmatic to a fault; will sell anything to anyone if the price is right.
Treats denying payouts as an art form and views tragedy strictly as a liability.
Opportunistic wreck looters flying barely-functional scrap.
A heavily armed corporate courier disguised as a civilian freighter.
A sprawling orbital junkyard filled with the stripped husks of dead ships.
A massive insurance conglomerate that holds policies on half the sector's ships.

public_situation: A beloved local pilot died when their ship broke apart in deep space. The {role:underwriters_guild} is refusing to pay the life insurance, citing pilot error.
private_truth: The ship suffered a catastrophic part failure. The insurance company knows this and is buying up the salvage to hide the evidence.

beats.public_change: The {role:salvage_yard} recovers the wreck and puts the telemetry drive up for auction.

missions.reason: Scavengers stole the telemetry drive before the salvage boss could secure it. He hires the pilot to blow them up and get it back.
missions.private_fact: The scavengers' comms chatter reveals they were hired by the insurance company to steal the drive.

beats.public_change: The salvage boss gets the drive back and immediately accepts a massive preemptive bid from the {role:underwriters_guild}.

missions.reason: The child desperately needs silicate to trade for the drive before the insurance company takes it. They hire the pilot to mine and deliver it.
missions.private_fact: The salvage boss takes the ore as a down payment, but admits the insurance company's courier is already inbound to collect the drive.

beats.public_change: The insurance company's courier departs with the drive to permanently bury the truth.

missions.reason: The child pays the pilot to destroy the courier and recover the telemetry drive from the wreckage.
missions.private_fact: The insurance agent immediately contacts the pilot, demanding they hand over the drive for a 'reward' once they pick it up.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot has the telemetry drive. The child is waiting for it, but the insurance agent is offering a massive bribe to hand it over to them instead.

options.label: Give the drive to the grieving child
Sell the drive to the insurance agent

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot recovers the drive and gives it to the child.
resolutions.summary: The unedited telemetry proves mechanical failure. The insurance company is forced to pay out the life insurance, clearing the deceased pilot's name.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot blew up a corporate courier to prove a crash wasn't pilot error.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot recovers the drive and sells it to the insurance agent.
resolutions.summary: The insurance agent destroys the drive. The crash is officially ruled pilot error, the family is left destitute, and the pilot gets rich.
The courier safely delivers the drive to the underwriters' vault. The child runs out of money and is forced to drop the dispute.

loose_threads.detail: The failed engine manifold on the wreck has a serial number that matches a batch recalled three years ago, but it looks brand new.
The insurance agent complains about being transferred to this sector as a punishment for 'asking too many questions' back home.

radio_hooks: {role:underwriters_guild} formally denies payout for recent local tragedy.
Scavengers spotted picking over the remains of a beloved pilot's ship.

voice_direction.grieving_child: Exhausted but fiercely determined. Voice shakes with suppressed anger, never with tears.
voice_direction.salvage_boss: Gruff, pragmatic, speaks in short, transactional sentences.
voice_direction.insurance_agent: Polite, oily, uses dense corporate jargon to sound completely reasonable while being deeply cruel.
